# Mermaid: the export, the import, and the limits of both

Generated from `mermaid_out.py` and `mermaid_in.py`. Two jobs: a Mermaid export that renders
natively on GitHub and re-imports without loss, and an import of what people actually write.
Everything here is deterministic and offline; no model call, no network, no rendering of the
input.

## Export (`cairn diagram to-mermaid <file>`)

A view becomes a flowchart, or a `sequenceDiagram` for a flow. Every element, arrow, boundary
and message also appears as a `%% cairn` JSON comment, and those comments are the real payload:
the picture is for a reader, the comments are what makes the round trip lossless. Colours come
from the token file's `%%{init: ...}%%` line, so an export never carries styling of its own.

A label cannot break out. Every character Mermaid or HTML could act on becomes a numeric entity,
so no name can close a node, start a `%%` directive, add an edge, attach a click handler or open
a tag. Ids that Mermaid cannot carry (reserved words, spaces, duplicates after sanitising) are
renamed in the drawing and travel in the comments.

### Shapes per element type

| Type | Token shape | Mermaid shape |
|---|---|---|
| `person` | person | `(["` … `"])` |
| `system` | box | `["` … `"]` |
| `external-system` | box | `["` … `"]` |
| `container` | box | `["` … `"]` |
| `data-store` | cylinder | `[("` … `")]` |
| `channel` | pipe | `[["` … `"]]` |
| `library` | library | `[/"` … `"/]` |
| `component` | component | `["` … `"]` |
| `code` | compartment | `["` … `"]` |
| `entity` | compartment | `["` … `"]` |
| `state` | pill | `("` … `")` |

## Import (`cairn diagram from-mermaid <file>`)

A flowchart subset, `sequenceDiagram` for flows, and Mermaid's C4 syntax. Nothing is evaluated:
the text is scanned line by line and only recognised constructs are read.

What the importer reads:

- flowcharts and `graph`: nodes, every standard shape, labels with `<br/>` parts, `[technology]`
  parts and `data:` classes, plain and thick and dotted lines, `-- text -->` and `|label|`
  labels, chained edges (`a --> b --> c`), `&` fan-out, two-headed arrows, `subgraph` boundaries
  (`name ["Title · type"]`), and `direction`
- `sequenceDiagram`: `participant` and `actor` (with `as`), message arrows (`->>`, `-->>`, `--)`,
  `--x`), fragments (`alt`/`else`, `opt`, `loop`, `par`/`and`, `critical`, `break`), `rect`,
  `title`, `box`, activations and `autonumber`
- C4: `Person`, `System`, `System_Ext`, the database and queue variants, `Container`, `Component`,
  `Boundary` and the three system boundaries, `Rel` with every directional variant, `BiRel`,
  `C4Context`, `C4Container`, `C4Component`, `C4Dynamic` and `C4Deployment`

### Supplying the facts the picture cannot carry

A hand-drawn chart has shapes and arrows but no technology, responsibility, evidence or
provenance. Those come from `%% cairn` comments, in a short form for people:

```
%% cairn api type=container tech="Python · FastAPI" evidence="shop-api/main.py:3"
%% cairn api->db how="SQL" style=sync
%% cairn diagram kind=container title="Containers of Shop" scope="Shop"
```

or in the full JSON form that `to-mermaid` writes, where a comment replaces the text entirely

rather than merging with it:

```
%% cairn:element api {"type":"container","tech":"Python","evidence":["shop-api/main.py:3"]}
%% cairn:boundary shop {"id":"shop","name":"Shop","type":"software system"}
%% cairn:rel api->db {"what":"Reads and writes orders","how":"SQL"}
%% cairn:msg 3 {"from":"api","to":"db","how":"SQL"}
```

A title can also come from a `--- title: "…" ---` front matter block, which is what an export
writes. `title` inside a flowchart body is not Mermaid and is reported.

### What the importer ignores, and says so

| Syntax | What happens |
|---|---|
| `classDef`, `class`, `style`, `linkStyle` | styling; ignored and counted in one warning |
| `click`, `callback`, `href`, `link`, `links` | interactions; never evaluated, never followed |
| `direction`, `accTitle`, `accDescr` | layout and accessibility text with no place in a description |
| nested subgraphs | flattened: boundaries do not nest |
| arrows to or from a subgraph | dropped: a boundary is not an endpoint |
| `note` | dropped: the evidence table carries what a note would have said |
| `%%` comments that are not `%% cairn` | ignored silently; they are for the reader, not the model |
| `%%{init: ...}%%` | ignored; colours come from the token file, not from the file |

Nothing is ever executed: no click handler, callback, link or style is followed, and an
unreadable chart is a warning, not a silent partial answer. **Any fact the importer cannot
represent is returned as a warning**, including a `%% cairn` comment that matches no node,
arrow or message: a comment that vanishes quietly is the one failure mode that would make a
hand-made diagram lie about itself.

## Limits

The importer is bounded by the same limits as the rest of the diagram pipeline, so a hostile
file cannot cost anything:

| Limit | Value | Refused how |
|---|---|---|
| File size | 2,000,000 bytes | `MermaidError`, before any parsing |
| Lines | 5,000 | `MermaidError` |
| Characters in one line | 20,000 | the line is dropped, with a warning |
| Nodes | 5,000 | `MermaidError` |
| Arrows | 20,000 | `MermaidError` |
| Warnings | 100 | the rest are counted, not listed |
| Binary data | any NUL byte | `MermaidError` |

## Round trip

```
cairn diagram to-mermaid view.yaml   > view.mmd    # facts in %% cairn comments
cairn diagram from-mermaid view.mmd  > view.yaml   # the same description back
```

`tests/system/test_mermaid_golden.py` proves the round trip on every published example, on the
computed views of the offline fixture products, and on a corpus of hand-written charts in
`tests/system/fixtures/mermaid/` that must import with warnings rather than a crash. The exports
are also rendered by the real Mermaid CLI in CI (`.github/workflows/diagrams.yml`), because
"Cairn can parse it" is not the same claim as "Mermaid can render it".
